To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microtubule inhibitors, colchicine and vincristine, cause an inhibition of the output of total proteins into bile, with the various protein components showing different time courses of change, and that the biliary output and the plasma levels of albumin are increased by the administration of these drugs.
the biliary output, in the bile-fistula rat, of alkaline phosphodiesterases I and A, immunoglobulins A and M, and albumin, are all affected by colchicine and, to a lesser extent, by vinblastine.
the output of total protein into bile was reduced by both colchicine and by vinblastine, but the various protein components of the bile showed different patterns of response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the microtubules of the bile-duct epithelium and their relation to the biliary secretion of proteins.
the mechanism of the output of proteins, including albumin and immunoglobulins, into bile.
the mechanism of protein output into the bile and the repair process in the bile canals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microtubules have a role in the transport of plasma-membrane components into bile, but that this role is not a simple one and that other factors must be involved.

the biliary output (and therefore the rate of secretion into bile) of the various plasma-membrane proteins (alkaline phosphodiesterases, immunoglobulins and albumin) is differentially affected by the microtubule inhibitors colchicine and/or vinblastine.
the microtubule inhibitors cause a reduction in the output of proteins, but that this is a complex process involving different proteins and different times after drug administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
colchicine, by its effects on microtubules in bile-duct epithelial cells, causes a change in the output of proteins from the plasma membrane.
colchicine and vincristine cause an impairment in the output of proteins from liver cells into bile.

microtubule disruption by colchicine and/or vinblastine caused: (a) an increase in the biliary concentration of albumin and (b) a decrease in the biliary concentrations of alkaline phosphodiesterases I and II, immunoglobulins A and E, and alpha 2-macroglobulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
colchicine, vinblastine, and vincristine, at the doses used here, are not cytolytic to the bile canaliculi.
the microtubule system is involved in the secretion of proteins into bile.
the output of proteins from the liver into the bile is a complex process, which can be altered in different ways by different drugs.
